speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. When did your fever start, and are you experiencing any pain or discharge from your C-section incision or perineum?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any pain or burning sensation when you urinate, and has your fever spiked above 100.4°F (38°C)? I need to know if you have noticed any foul-smelling vaginal discharge to help distinguish between endometritis and a urinary tract infection.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the uterine tenderness and prolonged labor, postpartum endometritis is highly suspected, though the urinary symptoms are concerning. Let's confirm the diagnosis with laboratory evidence. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Urinalysis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC Pending, Hemoglobin Pending, Platelets Pending; Urinalysis: Appearance Pending, WBC Pending, RBC Pending, Nitrites Pending, Leukocyte_Esterase Pending

speaker: Doctor
text: While we await the lab results, I need to clarify if you are experiencing any nausea, vomiting, or constipation, as these could suggest an ileus related to the infection. Have you also noticed any changes in your lochia, such as a foul odor or an increase in amount?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Uncomplicated pregnancy leading up to a vaginal delivery. No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: Does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. Lives with her partner.

speaker: Doctor
text: The uterine tenderness, fever, and prolonged labor strongly point to postpartum endometritis, a common infection of the uterine lining. I will proceed with the diagnosis based on these classic clinical findings. DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum Endometritis
